name: Uyghurs
summary: The Chinese government is carrying out a campaign of mass detention, forced labor, cultural erasure, and surveillance against Uyghur Muslims and other Turkic minorities in Xinjiang. Experts and governments have described the situation as genocide and crimes against humanity.
context:
Since 2017, the Chinese government has built a vast network of internment camps in Xinjiang (which Uyghurs call East Turkestan), detaining an estimated 1 to 1.8 million Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims. China describes these as "vocational education and training centers," but extensive reporting, leaked government documents, and survivor testimony reveal a system of arbitrary mass detention.

Detainees have described forced political indoctrination, torture, sexual violence, forced sterilization, and coerced labor. Birth rates in Uyghur-majority areas of Xinjiang have plummeted — dropping by over 80% in some counties between 2015 and 2018, according to Chinese government statistics analyzed by researchers.

Beyond the camps, the Uyghur population faces pervasive surveillance through AI-powered cameras, mandatory smartphone apps, DNA collection, and a system of assigned government "minders" who live in Uyghur homes. Mosques have been demolished or repurposed, religious practices restricted, and Uyghur language education curtailed.

Forced labor is another critical dimension. Reports from the Australian Strategic Policy Institute, the BBC, and others have documented Uyghur workers being transferred to factories across China under coercive conditions, producing goods for major global brands in textiles, electronics, and agriculture — including cotton, polysilicon for solar panels, and tomato products.

The UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights released a landmark assessment in 2022 concluding that China's actions in Xinjiang may constitute crimes against humanity. Several governments, including the United States, Canada, the UK, and the Netherlands, have formally recognized the situation as genocide.

China denies all allegations and has blocked independent access to the region, making documentation difficult but not impossible thanks to the courageous work of diaspora Uyghurs, investigative journalists, and researchers analyzing satellite imagery and leaked documents.

donate.name: Uyghur Human Rights Project
donate.description: Leading research and advocacy organization documenting abuses and promoting Uyghur rights through policy engagement.

donate.name: Campaign for Uyghurs
donate.description: Grassroots advocacy organization led by Uyghurs, focused on awareness campaigns and political lobbying for accountability.

awareness: Learn about forced labor supply chains — check if brands you buy from have been linked to Uyghur forced labor using the Coalition to End Forced Labour in the Uyghur Region's resources
Share the stories of Uyghur survivors who have testified about their experiences in the camps
Organize campus or community film screenings of documentaries covering the Uyghur crisis
Follow Uyghur activists and diaspora organizations on social media to amplify their advocacy
Educate yourself and others about the surveillance technology being tested on Uyghurs that is being exported to other authoritarian regimes worldwide
political: Urge your representatives to support the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) and its strict enforcement against imports made with forced labor
Call for diplomatic actions including Magnitsky Act sanctions against Chinese officials responsible for the detention and surveillance system
Support resolutions recognizing the situation in Xinjiang as genocide and crimes against humanity
Advocate for granting asylum and refugee status to Uyghurs fleeing persecution
Push corporations and pension funds to divest from companies complicit in surveillance and forced labor in Xinjiang
